instructions: Fill a large pot with water, add 1 tbsp of the salt and bring it to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, pat the chicken dry. Season both sides with 1/2 tsp of the salt and a little of the pepper. Slice the mushrooms, chop the green onions (white and green parts) and mince the garlic.
Cook the linguine in the boiling water until it's al dente, about 10 minutes. Drain it and leave it in the colander.
Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat. Add the chicken and cook for 5 minutes, until the underside is golden.

Flip the chicken, cover the pan and cook for 5 to 6 minutes. You're cooking it to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest part: it's done when there's no pink left.
Transfer the chicken to a cutting board and let it rest for 5 minutes, then slice it into strips.

Add the last 1 tbsp of oil to the same skillet over medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms and green onions and cook for 6 to 7 minutes, stirring now and then, until they're soft and golden. Transfer them to a bowl.
Turn the heat down to medium and melt the butter in the same skillet. Add the flour and garlic and stir for 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in the broth, then the milk, so there are no lumps. Simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until the sauce is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Stir in the spinach, the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and a pinch of pepper. Cook for about 1 minute, until the spinach has wilted.
Add the chicken, mushrooms and linguine and toss for 1 minute, until everything is coated and hot. Taste it and add a pinch more salt if it's flat.
Serve with the Parmesan sprinkled over each bowl.
method_notes: Natasha's Kitchen leads (4.98 from 67): a flour and butter base thinned with broth and milk, so the sauce is light and creamy rather than a heavy cream sauce, with mushrooms and green onions cooked in the chicken pan. Other Florentine pages vary in the sauce (sun-dried tomato, pesto Alfredo), but the lead's version is the plainest and matches the list line. It kept to about 40 minutes at a real stove.
